strategy_definition.summary: SMT divergence identifies cracks in correlation between closely correlated pairs (e.g., ES/NQ or EURUSD/GBPUSD) to confirm entry when price taps an existing higher-timeframe PD array. It serves strictly as an entry confirmation tool rather than a bias indicator.

timeframes.notes: Fractal application. Demonstrated using 4-hour and Daily higher-timeframe PD arrays (FVGs, OBs) with lower-timeframe execution.

glossary.SMT: Smart Money Technique - a crack in correlation where two normally correlated assets fail to make corresponding swing highs or lows at the same time.
glossary.Crack in correlation: When two correlated assets (e.g., ES and NQ) fail to move in sync, indicating underlying institutional orders being placed in the market.
glossary.Buying on strength technique: An entry technique for turtle soup setups where a buy stop is placed above the high of the specific candle responsible for sweeping the swing low.

custom_signals.name: bullish_smt_divergence
custom_signals.plain_definition: Between two positively correlated instruments, one instrument makes a lower swing low (or sweeps a swing low) while the other instrument fails to sweep and makes a higher swing low.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: Asset_A.swing_low[1].price < Asset_A.swing_low[0].price AND Asset_B.swing_low[1].price > Asset_B.swing_low[0].price across identical time timestamps

custom_signals.name: buying_on_strength_trigger
custom_signals.plain_definition: A buy stop trigger set at the high of the individual candle that swept the previous swing low.

sequence: Establish a higher-timeframe directional bias and locate an active HTF PD array (e.g., FVG or Order Block).
Monitor price entering the HTF PD array on the traded instrument alongside a closely correlated instrument (e.g., ES with NQ, or GBPUSD with EURUSD).

Observe an SMT divergence: in a bullish scenario, one instrument sweeps a prior swing low (lower low / breaker pattern), while the correlated instrument fails to take its low (higher low / swing failure pattern).
Identify the strength leader on a higher timeframe basis to decide which instrument to trade.
Execute using the 'Buying on strength' technique by placing a buy stop above the high of the sweeping candle, or wait for standard lower-timeframe entry confirmation patterns.

invalidation.text: If both correlated assets make symmetrical swing lows without a crack in correlation, no SMT divergence exists.

filters.text: Do not use SMT as a directional bias tool; use it solely as a late confirmation tool after HTF bias and PD arrays are determined.
Only compare swing lows when bullish; only compare swing highs when bearish.
Execute on the strength leader on a higher-timeframe basis rather than selecting a pair based purely on SMT.

entry_rule.text: Place a buy stop order above the high of the candle responsible for sweeping the swing low ('Buying on strength technique'), or enter on a subsequent lower-timeframe entry pattern.
entry_rule.quote: the candle that was responsible for coming back below that low that exactly there would be your entry

target_rule.text: Target opposing swing highs or higher-timeframe discount/premium arrays (such as an order block or FVG).
target_rule.quote: overlapping with what right here an order block this is our last line of defense this could be our Target

stop_rule.text: Place stop loss below the low of the sweep, giving it breathing room (e.g., 6 points on NQ) rather than suffocating the stop.
stop_rule.quote: give it some room give it some room to breathe don't suffocate your stop loss so in this case what you could do is say all right give it six points

management.notes: Turtle soup entries can call the exact bottom/top, but waiting for standard secondary confirmation allows for more refined stop losses.

presenter_claims.claim: SMT provides high-probability entry confirmation because cracks in correlation reflect underlying institutional orders being placed.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price on ES trades down into a 4-hour fair value gap.
Overlay of NQ candles is added to compare swing lows with ES.
NQ sweeps a prior swing low to print a lower low, whereas ES holds and prints a higher low, forming a bullish SMT divergence.
A subsequent swing low forms another SMT divergence where NQ sweeps lower and ES prints another higher low.
Buying on strength entry: a buy stop order is placed above the high of the red candle responsible for sweeping the low on NQ.
Stop loss is placed 6 points below the low of the sweep to give the trade breathing room.

chart_examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter cautions against using SMT as a directional bias tool, stating it will severely confuse the trader. Instead, it must serve solely as a confirmation tool inside an existing HTF PD array. When executing turtle soup SMT entries on the HTF strength leader (NQ), he demonstrates the 'buying on strength' technique above the sweeping candle with an explicit 6-point stop buffer.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: GBPUSD reaches a Daily fair value gap overlapping a Daily order block.
EURUSD candle overlay is added to evaluate swing lows against GBPUSD.
EURUSD prints a swing failure pattern (higher low) while GBPUSD sweeps its prior swing low (breaker pattern), marking the first SMT.
A subsequent leg shows GBPUSD sweeping another low while EURUSD again fails to break lower, confirming a double SMT divergence.
Presenter notes that 'buying on strength' was challenging here because price kept drifting down without triggering buy stops until standard entry models appeared later.

chart_examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter demonstrates double bullish SMT divergence on Forex pairs (GU and EU) inside a Daily FVG/OB zone. He explains the trade-selection dilemma between buying the manipulated pair (GU) versus the stronger pair (EU), recommending execution on whichever asset exhibits greater higher-timeframe relative strength. He also highlights that turtle soup entries can require waiting for standard lower-timeframe confirmations when prices grind continuously lower.
